clue.text: A second, so great in itself

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second, as in units of time
such, as in 'such a fuss', means so great

explanation.surface: Something lasting a single second is described as grand in its own right, a puzzling boast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean considered intrinsically, in the strict sense of the thing itself.

clue.text: Supplementary material inserted that may have to be taken out?

definitions.meaning: extra matter attached at the back of a book or report

definitions.text: inserted that may have to be taken out?
definitions.meaning: the small organ in the gut that surgeons often remove, punning on material inserted into a text

explanation.surface: An editor wonders whether added material slipped into a document will have to be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading switches from editing to surgery: the organ attached to the gut is the one routinely 'taken out'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an addendum at the end of a book and the vestigial organ often removed by surgeons.

clue.text: Curt type round hospital

indicators.note: round means the word for type goes around the hospital letter

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A brusque sort of person is found doing rounds of a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Being curt means being abrupt or brief with someone, a synonym.

clue.text: Elegant, a turn in show

parts.note: chic means stylish or elegant
a go is a turn, as in 'whose go is it?'

explanation.surface: A stylish performer takes a turn in a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kander and Ebb stage musical about Roxie Hart, an example of a show.

clue.text: Piece of writing found in small underground chapel, we're told

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: we're told signals that the chapel word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a crypt is a vault or chapel beneath a church

explanation.surface: A manuscript turns up in a little chapel below ground, or so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is a written text, such as a play's or film's lines, so a piece of writing.

clue.text: Old king circling stage in Worcester, perhaps

indicators.note: circling means the king's name goes around the stage word

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch walks round a theatre stage in the English city of Worcester.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcester looks like the city, but here it is Worcester College, Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester is one of the colleges of Oxford University, so an example of an academic institution.

clue.text: Run out in big limo abroad causes complicated situation

indicators.note: in places the run-out letters within the rearranged limo letters
abroad suggests the letters of big limo are scattered widely

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A batsman dismissed inside a large overseas limousine creates a tangled mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges the limo letters to IMBGLIO; 'Run out' is the cricket scorecard shorthand, and 'in' sets it into that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is an embarrassing or confused muddle, a tangled state of affairs.

clue.text: Samovar's odd nature

definitions.note: read as 'Samovar is', a Russian vessel for boiling water for tea

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of nature are made strange and rearranged

explanation.surface: A samovar has a curious character.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a large Russian metal pot heated to keep water hot for brewing, a type of this vessel.

clue.text: Against modelling after work

indicators.note: after places the modelling word following the work abbreviation

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
posing is what a model does when modelling

explanation.surface: Someone objects to taking up modelling once the day job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing means resisting or contrary to, the same sense as against.

clue.text: First in emergency to enter ravine over bridge gets bravery award

indicators.note: over places the ravine part above the bridge part in this down answer
to enter means the emergency letter goes inside the ravine word

parts.note: a gorge is a narrow steep-sided ravine

indicators.note: first in takes the opening letter of emergency

parts.note: to cross is to bridge or span a gap

explanation.surface: A rescuer dashes into a ravine and over a bridge, and is decorated for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: The George Cross is the highest British civilian decoration for gallantry, so a medal for courage.

clue.text: One from Tripoli, perhaps hidden in Tripoli by another

indicators.note: hidden in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A person from Tripoli may be concealed in Tripoli by somebody else.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, so someone from there is a national of that North African country.

clue.text: Decorative bow tie

definitions.meaning: an ornamental bow of ribbon or cord, a loop tied for show
to fasten by looping string or rope

explanation.surface: A neat bow tie worn for decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an ornamental bow and to fasten cord by intertwining it.

clue.text: Best place for a surfer, out in the open

definitions.meaning: read literally, on top of the surfboard rather than underwater
honest and legitimate, with nothing concealed

explanation.surface: Advice on where a surfer should be, in plain sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase literally: a surfer wants to stay on top of the plank.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means honest and open, with nothing hidden, the original sense being cards held above the gaming table.

clue.text: Be extremely logical after fight evokes nursery rhyme

indicators.note: after places the be-and-logical letters following the fight word

parts.note: a ding-dong is a heated fight or argument
taken as written

indicators.note: extremely takes the outermost letters of the word logical

explanation.surface: Being thoroughly rational after a scrap brings a children's verse to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's verse about the pussy in the well is a well-known nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Complaining, leader of gang on unmasking

indicators.note: on places the gang letter above the unmasking word in this down answer
leader of takes the front letter of the word gang

parts.note: rumbling, in British slang, means finding someone out or seeing through them

explanation.surface: A gang boss moans about being exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumbling means muttering discontentedly, a synonym of complaining.

clue.text: Potter married suitable wife inside

parts.note: to wed is to marry, so wed means married

indicators.note: inside means the wife letter goes within the suitable word

parts.note: good can mean suitable or fit, as in 'a good time to call'

explanation.surface: A man who makes pottery wed a fitting partner and keeps her at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Josiah Wedgwood was the famous English potter whose firm made jasperware.

clue.text: Ill-natured individual, most cruel guy when upset

indicators.note: upset means the letters of most cruel guy are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty person is the cruellest chap when riled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for an unpleasant, aggressive or dangerous person.

clue.text: Dog taken from pitch, about to be brought over

parts.note: to lurch is to pitch or roll suddenly, like a ship

indicators.note: brought over means the about word is turned upward in this down answer

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letters

explanation.surface: A dog removed from a sports field is about to be fetched across.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred dog, typically greyhound with collie or terrier, used for hunting.

clue.text: Sheer, the Parisian church tower

parts.note: steep and sheer both describe a near-vertical slope
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A sheer-sided Paris church has a tall tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tower with a spire on a church building.

clue.text: Postpone draw? About to

indicators.note: about means the draw word goes around the word to

parts.note: a puff is a draw on a cigarette or pipe

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture ends level, and it is about to be postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' looks like a tied match but is a puff on a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off something is to defer or delay it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Seeing off rum, becomes awkward

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of rum and becomes are spoiled and mixed up

explanation.surface: Watching someone dispose of the rum, things become uncomfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing' is just a link; 'off' rearranges RUM plus BECOMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbersome means unwieldy or clumsy, hard to handle, much like awkward.

clue.text: Clothes son obtained in recession

indicators.note: in recession means the son and obtained letters go into retreat, read backwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees
got means obtained

explanation.surface: A son gets new clothes during an economic downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Togs is informal British slang for clothes or outfits, from toga.

clue.text: Short in toaster's electrics

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words toaster's electrics

explanation.surface: A short circuit occurs in a toaster's wiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' suggests a short circuit but means brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief or abrupt in speech, so short.

clue.text: Beeswax, for example, from one of the EU countries

definitions.meaning: beeswax is a substance used to shine furniture

definitions.text: from one of the EU countries
definitions.meaning: of the people of Poland, an EU member

explanation.surface: Beeswax sourced from a European Union nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a shining wax and, capitalised, belonging to Poland.

clue.text: Excellent Brazilian city toured by American caretaker

indicators.note: toured by means the city sits inside the caretaker word, which goes around it

parts.note: super is American shorthand for a building superintendent or caretaker
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A US janitor takes a holiday tour of a Brazilian city and finds it superb.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior means of higher quality, so first-rate or excellent.

clue.text: Guess shape

definitions.meaning: to work something out or reckon
a form or outline, as in a human silhouette

explanation.surface: Guess the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to reckon or suppose, and also a body's outline or form.

clue.text: On purpose, making motto

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
an end is a purpose or aim, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: Doing something deliberately produces a slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On purpose' reads as deliberately but splits into two pieces; on and leg are cricket's names for the same side of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend can be an inscription or caption on a coin or crest, such as its motto.
